silently.linePrev: How terribly strange to be seventy
silently.line: Old friends, memory brushes the same years, silently sharing the same fears
stanza: 1 ContributorOld Friends LyricsOld friends, old friends sat on their parkbench…
A newspaper blowin' through the grass
Falls on the round toes of the high shoes of the old friends
Old friends, winter companions, the old men
Lost in their overcoats, waiting for the sun
The sounds of the city sifting through trees
Settles like dust on the shoulders of the old friends
Can you imagine us years from today, sharing a parkbench quietly
How terribly strange to be seventy
Old friends, memory brushes the same years, silently sharing the same fears

stanza: I see the blossoms broke and wet after the rain
Little sister, he will be back again
I have washed a thousand spiders down the drain

In tiny nooses, safe from everyone —
Nothing but a nuisance; gone now, dead and done —
Be a woman. Be a woman
This day was once
(Silently full)

Can't wait at all
(Can't wait at all)

stanza: And did you know the Liberty Bell is a replica
Silently housed in its original walls

silently.linePrev: Wednesday morning at 5 o'clock as the day begins
silently.lineNext: Leaving the note that she hoped would say more
stanza: Wednesday morning at 5 o'clock as the day begins
Silently closing her bedroom door
Leaving the note that she hoped would say more
She goes downstairs to the kitchen clutching her handkerchief
Quietly turning the backdoor key
Stepping outside, she is free
